label: Inaugurated contemporary virtue ethics
description: In 'Modern Moral Philosophy' (1958), Anscombe proposed that moral obligation concepts ('ought') are psychologically incoherent without divine law, demanding a return to Aristotelian virtue and human flourishing.
historicalContext: Published in Philosophy in 1958 during a period dominated by Oxford emotivism (Ayer) and prescriptivism (Hare).
dialecticalTension: Challenged the entire modern moral consensus by uniting Wittgensteinian linguistic philosophy with classical Aristotelian ethics.

citations.author: G. E. M. Anscombe
citations.quote: The concepts of obligation, and duty—moral obligation and moral duty, that is to say—and of what is morally right and wrong, ought to be jettisoned if this is psychologically possible.

label: Mentored Anscombe and shaped her philosophy of action and language
description: Anscombe was Wittgenstein's most devoted student, his chosen translator of Philosophical Investigations, and applied his method of philosophical psychology to intentional action.
historicalContext: Anscombe attended Wittgenstein's Cambridge seminars throughout the 1940s and lived in his house during his final illness.
dialecticalTension: Applied Wittgenstein's therapeutic critique of Cartesian private mental states to the concept of intentional action.

citations.author: G. E. M. Anscombe
citations.quote: What is the characteristic of intentional actions? It is that they are actions to which a certain sense of the question 'Why?' is given application.

label: Synthesized Aristotelian virtue ethics with analytic linguistic philosophy
description: Anscombe brought Aristotelian teleology, eudaimonia, and moral psychology back into the center of 20th-century analytic philosophy.
historicalContext: Replaced legalistic Kantian and utilitarian ethics with the Aristotelian question: what traits of character constitute human flourishing?
dialecticalTension: Demonstrated that Aristotelian virtue ethics provides a rigorous naturalistic basis for ethics without theological dogma.

citations.author: G. E. M. Anscombe
citations.quote: Aristotle does not have a concept of moral obligation in our modern sense. For him, virtue is a quality that enables a human being to function well qua human.

label: Collaborated to launch the Oxford virtue ethics renaissance
description: Anscombe and Foot worked closely at Oxford to dismantle non-cognitivism and reconstruct normative ethics around natural virtues and the doctrine of double effect.
historicalContext: The wartime and post-war Oxford circle of Anscombe, Foot, Murdoch, and Midgley formed the epicenter of late-20th-century ethical realism.
dialecticalTension: United virtue ethics with rigorous normative dilemmas and critiques of consequentialism.

citations.author: Philippa Foot
citations.quote: Anyone who has had the good fortune to discuss philosophical problems with Elizabeth Anscombe will know how deep is my debt to her.

citations.author: Clare Mac Cumhaill and Rachael Wiseman
citations.work: Metaphysical Animals: How Four Women Brought Philosophy Back to Life
